title: One hour of satellites over the northern Atacama Desert in Chile (October 2025)
caption: One hour of satellite trails above the Extremely Large Telescope, northern Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Many bright streaks cross the night sky above Chile's northern Atacama Desert in this image. It is a stack of frames from a time-lapse video filmed on 15 October 2025, starting roughly two hours after the Sun went down, and together they show the traffic overhead during just one hour.

A few of the trails were made by aeroplanes, easy to recognise from their blinking coloured lights. Most, though, are satellites crossing the sky. Each satellite catches sunlight and leaves a line across the frame as it moves, and stacking an hour's worth of frames shows how many pass over.

In the foreground stands the dome of ESO's Extremely Large Telescope, described as the world's largest optical and infrared telescope, still under construction on Cerro Armazones. Behind it, the lasers of ESO's Very Large Telescope shine from Paranal Observatory, 22 kilometres away.

understand.summary: This is a stack of frames from a time-lapse video covering one hour, as stated by ESO. The source gives no camera details.
understand.eye: Stacking an hour of frames shows every trail at once, whereas the eye would see each satellite only as a single moving point.
